candidates.title: Non-shared flash drive, NVRAM or replacement image shorter than the configured length is accepted and zero-padded, although the manual says the length must exactly match the image file size
candidates.component: Emulator core: machine creation and replace_memory_range (memory_address_range / os::mapped_memory backing_gap); cartesi-machine CLI --flash-drive, --nvram, --replace-memory-range
candidates.role: Honest operator for the core (machine creation and replace_memory_range are machine API), Support for the CLI
candidates.location: src/memory-address-range.cpp check_mmap_flags (.backing_gap = !backing_store.shared); src/os-mapped-memory.cpp mapped_memory::mapped_memory lines ~164-180 (a shorter backing file is accepted unless shared or !backing_gap); doc/README.md lines 733-737; CLI help src/cartesi-machine.lua line 248
candidates.description: doc/README.md (Flash drives) says: 'If, however, both length and data_filename are specified, then the length must exactly match the size of the image file referred to by the data_filename parameter.' The CLI help repeats it ('if length and filename are set, the image file size must match length'). In the implementation, a non-shared memory range whose image file is SHORTER than the configured length is accepted: os::mapped_memory maps the file and fills the rest of the range with anonymous zero pages (backing_gap). Only a longer file, or a shorter file for a shared range, is refused. The same applies to --replace-memory-range with a non-shared replacement. The resulting state is well defined (the image followed by zeros). Its hash is consistent across store, load, store with sharing none and a rebuild (checked), and it equals what cartesi-hash-tree-hash computes for the zero-padded file. So the contradiction does not produce a wrong hash.
candidates.trigger: The trusted caller (the operator or a template author) passes a configuration or replacement whose image file is shorter than the explicit length. No guest or third-party data is involved.
candidates.reachability: Reachable through the documented creation and replace options. It does not depend on any guest state.
candidates.rating_steps: 1 Out of scope: no exclusion applies outright. It is not a deliberate state change through the API (section 8 'The effect of a deliberate state change made through the machine API, when the API performs it as documented' does not apply, because the API does not do what the manual documents). 2 Role: core machine creation is in the honest-operator role ('storing, loading, cloning and syncing machines' and the rest of the machine API where a node plausibly calls it), and the CLI is support. 3 High/Medium cases: none matches. It is not a guest-visible architectural deviation (R7 covers 'the RISC-V specification and the devices as the manual documents them', and this is host-side configuration validation). It leaves no hash tree or directory inconsistent (the Medium case 'leaves the hash tree, the cached state of the machine or a stored directory inconsistent with the machine's contents (R9)' does not hold, as checked). Section 8 says 'A contradiction between the manual and the behavior on a security-relevant point is a defect in one of the two. It takes the severity it would have if the manual were right', but whether a short image is zero-padded or refused at creation has no bearing on any hash, proof or transition. 4 Critical: it breaks no rule at a reachable state. R4 ('A configuration that would not [yield a machine on which this rule holds] is rejected when the machine is created') is met, since the accepted machine behaves correctly. 5 Low: 'a real defect that violates no rule or obligation of this model'.
candidates.threat_to_goal: None to the goal. The behavior contradicts a documented refusal, so a template author who relies on the manual to catch a truncated image (for example a flash drive image cut short in transfer) gets a machine with silently zero-filled contents. The template's hash would then differ from the intended one, and this is visible only by comparing against the on-chain commitment.
candidates.evidence: Ran /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r7/MANCLIBASE/e2.lua: a flash drive with length=8192 and a 4096-byte data file is accepted. store/load and store(SHARING_NONE)/load with clear_hash_tree give the same root as the running machine. A 5000-byte image with no length is correctly refused (not a multiple of 4 KiB), and more than 8 drives are refused ('too many flash drives').
candidates.test_idea: Create a machine with flash_drive={{length=8192, backing_store={data_filename=<4096-byte file>}}} and assert that creation raises an error (manual behavior). Today it succeeds, so the test exits 1. Alternatively, if the code is right, the manual and the --help text must be fixed to say a shorter non-shared image is zero-padded.

not_covered: State hashes and proof options of the slice (--initial-hash/--final-hash examples are only read, --initial-proof/--final-proof are excluded by the angle). The printed example hashes of the manual were not reproduced (no Linux boot, given host load).

The interactive-session (-i) wall-clock behavior and the Linux guest side of flash drives (cartesi-init mounting, user:dapp ownership, --user=root, --append-init, readmmap/writemmap, the calculator template example) were checked only as far as the CLI builds the configuration. No Linux guest was run.

Remote machines: --remote-shutdown, --no-remote-destroy, --no-remote-create and --remote-fork were checked by reading src/cartesi-machine.lua and the jsonrpc shutdown/fork/load/store/clone/sync handlers only. No server was started. Noted but not reported (trivial): --remote-health-check combined with --remote-fork forks a server child before exiting and leaves it running.
JSON-RPC server-side store/load/clone/sync over the wire were not exercised (only read: they call the same core functions with SHARING_NONE as the load default).

Experiments run (all consistent with the manual, nothing to report): (e1) SHARING_NONE load, run, clear_hash_tree and destroy leave the directory byte-identical. clone_stored hard-links only the read-only data files (PMAs, a read-only flash drive), and a SHARING_ALL load with clear_hash_tree, run, destroy and sync of the clone leaves the source byte-identical, with the clone's cached and rebuilt roots equal. (e3) store with sharing none/config/all: cached root equals rebuilt root. (e4) explicit misaligned drive starts are refused. (e5, e6) SHARING_CONFIG with only the hash tree shared, or only a flash drive shared: after destroy and sync, cached root equals rebuilt root. (e7) a tampered template (data changed, caches untouched) cloned and loaded with SHARING_ALL and clear_hash_tree, then destroyed with no hash request (or after running) and synced: reload without a rebuild gives the rebuilt root, so the O1 rebuild persists across the CLI's 'once' mode reloads.

Checked by reading, no defect: the CLI's sharing/revert-mode/sync constraints (config needs none, all needs stored or none, sync needs a sharing mode, clone defaults to all), destroy-before-sync ordering in the local and remote exit paths, the --store '%h'/'%Nh' substitution, the refusal of existing directories (store, clone, load with clone), the archive_version check, and cartesi-machine-stored-hash (it loads with SHARING_NONE and recomputes dirty pages). --store intentionally runs before an interrupted input's snapshot is reverted (the code comment says so), so --store and --final-hash show the interrupted machine while a stored revert-mode directory ends at the last commit. This is a manual nuance ('stored as it was right before cartesi-machine returns'), not reported.

Not covered: Windows/macOS persistence paths, reflink filesystems (the host is ext4, so reflinks fall back to copies), big-endian or 16 KiB-page hosts for directories 'transferred to other hosts', and --create (outside the manual slice) beyond noting that create-with-directory leaves the PMA data file writable whereas store marks it read-only (harmless, so clone reflinks it instead of hard-linking).
--dump-constants was read only (negative Lua integers are printed as 0x%x, strings single-quoted with escaping).
